We'll be rolling out a new-and-improved version of Expected Fantasy Points (XFP) this year @FantasyPtsData.

New to XFP this year:

- It works for QBs!
- It works for different scoring settings!
- It knows whether a target was catchable/accurate!

What is XFP? It's a model that predicts how many fantasy points an "average" player would score on each specific play. 

A carry at the 2-yard line with 8:00 minutes remaining in the 3rd quarter and the score tied is worth more than a 1st-and-10 carry at the 45-yard line with 1:30 left in the 4th quarter with a 24-10 lead.

One has a great chance of resulting in a rushing TD, and the other may gain a few yards at most to salt the clock away. They both go into the box score as 1 rush attempt, but XFP knows the former is much more valuable for fantasy than the latter.

We can say the same of a catchable target near the end zone vs. an uncatchable target at midfield. Or of a deep pass to a receiver with a +2 separation score on the play vs. a checkdown. 

By incorporating all of the standardized context our film charters record from watching every play, we've created a stat that's more predictive of next week's fantasy points than fantasy points are of themselves.

As always, I'll be incorporating XFP extensively within The Everything Report for subscribers each week!
